newsitem.title: CHINA: China vows to control labour exports to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China vows to control labour exports to Hong Kong.

text.p: China has vowed to keep strict control of labour exports from the mainland to the former British colony of Hong Kong, which returned to Beijing rule last week, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Rules governing the movement of workers to Hong Kong would be unchanged after the July 1 transfer of sovereignty from London, the official newspaper quoted Tang Zhixin of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying.
"The mainland will not take unilateral action to send workers to Hong Kong without consulting the government of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region," Tang said.
Beijing has promised Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy in political and economic affairs for 50 years after the capitalist enclave's return to the communist-ruled mainland.
Beijing wanted to set up a consulting mechanism with the Hong Kong government to exchange information on labour policies, Tang said.
Since 1989, when the mainland started to export workers to Hong Kong, about 60,000 had been employed in the region, the Business Weekly said.
About 28,000 mainland workers were employed in Hong Kong's retail, wholesale, trade, restaurant, textile, finance and other sectors, the newspaper said.
